# Make card packs available in the browser distribution

**Discovered from:** `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import)

## Problem statement

The card-pack (DLC) channel works under the Electron launcher but is **inert in
the browser distribution** (the GitHub Pages site at
`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`). In a plain browser the
Card Packs panel opens but always shows "No card packs installed", so the
production residential pack can neither be seen, unlocked, nor played. This
item bundles the production pack into the web distribution and adds a browser
content-unlock client so the whole **lock → purchase → enable → deal** path
works without a launcher content directory.

## Users

- **Browser player** — plays the distributed web build and expects the
  residential DLC to appear, be purchasable and playable.
- **Developer / pack author** — ships a pack and expects the web build to
  bundle it automatically, with no manual `<contentDir>` install step.

Example user stories:

> As a player of the web build, I want the residential card pack to appear in
> the Card Packs panel and be unlockable and playable, so the DLC works in the
> distributed browser version and not only under the Electron launcher.

> As a developer, I want the packs bundled into the web build automatically, so
> shipping a pack needs no manual content-directory install step.

## Existing state

- `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks()` reads the content directory from
  `window.tce.contentDir` (set only by the Electron preload from
  `TCE_RESOLVED_CONTENT_DIR`). In the browser that is `null`, so
  `shouldBootstrapPacks` (`src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`)
  returns `false` and `getMainStreetCardPackLoadResult()` stays `null`.
- Pack content lives in `packs/` (source) and is built into the gitignored
  `build/card-packs/packs/`, which a human must copy into
  `<contentDir>/packs/`. Nothing in the web build (`npm run build` → `dist/`)
  includes it.
- Two further Electron-only seams gate the browser path:
  - `resolveCardPackAssetUrl` (`core/src/ui/card-pack-url.ts`) builds pack
    URLs as `tce-packs://<gameId>/<packId>/<path>`; the scheme is served only
    by the Electron `pack-protocol` handler. The core loader
    (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`) uses this builder for the pack CSV as
    well as its assets, so the browser cannot read the CSV through it.
  - Content-unlock reads go through `window.tce.contentUnlocks`
    (`core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`); the total client degrades to
    "not unlocked" with no bridge, so even a discovered pack would render
    **locked** with no way to purchase it.
- The launcher content-directory install path (`packs/` → `build/card-packs/`
  → `<contentDir>/packs/`) already works under Electron and must keep working.

## Desired change

Adopt a **pack-source registry** so pack content is resolved from one of
several interchangeable sources rather than hard-wiring the Electron content
directory:

1. **Bundled (build-time) source** — implemented in this item (Option B or C
   below; the implementer records the final shape).
2. **Same-origin static `<base>/packs/`** and **remote URL source** — additive,
   future sources (remote hosting tracked separately by
   `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).

Alongside the bundled source, add a **`localStorage`-backed browser
content-unlock client** (reusing the `StorageLike` seam in
`src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`) plus a client-side **rule-scoped simulated-purchase**
rule, so the browser preserves the full lock → purchase → enable flow and the
unlock survives a reload.

### Locked direction (producer, 2026-10-10)

Producer confirmed the source-registry refinement and locked the direction:

- Build the **pack-source registry abstraction** now; the bundled source is
  implemented in this item; remote hosting is the linked follow-up
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (which depends on this item).
- **Bundled source = Option B (virtual registry) or Option C
  (`import.meta.glob`)** — the exact mechanism is an implementation detail for
  the implementer.
- **Browser content unlocks = `localStorage`-backed client** preserving the
  lock → purchase → enable flow.

### Options considered (design record)

- **Option A — static `public/packs/` + same-origin fallback contentDir.**
  Copy `packs/` into `public/packs/`; when `window.tce.contentDir` is absent
  fall back to `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`/`document.baseURI`. Reuses the fetch
  loader unchanged, closest parity with Electron, packs updatable without a JS
  rebuild — but needs a prebuild copy step and a browser equivalent of the
  `tce-packs://` asset URL builder.
- **Option B — build-time virtual pack registry.** A Vite plugin (mirroring
  `gameDiscoveryPlugin` / `virtual:game-registry`) scans `packs/` and emits a
  virtual module; Main Street injects `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv` transports
  that read from it. Offline, deterministic, follows an established repo
  pattern — but bakes packs into the bundle and needs a plugin + types.
- **Option C — inline `import.meta.glob` bundling (no plugin).** A small
  `bundledPacks.ts` uses `import.meta.glob('../../packs/**/*', …)` for the
  manifest/CSV (`?raw`) and assets (`?url`). No plugin, simplest to implement,
  works in browser and tests — but always bundles every pack (bundle size
  grows) and is Vite-specific.
- **Option D — pre-merge the pack CSV into the base pool at build time.**
  Simple, but loses the DLC gate semantics and does not satisfy the
  "demonstrate the unlock path" intent of `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`. Rejected.
- **Option E — sibling deployed packs directory.** Mechanically Option A with
  packs as a separate deployment artefact. Still available as a future source.

**Recommendation:** Option C (or B) for the bundled source, unified behind the
pack-source registry, combined with the `localStorage`-backed content-unlock
client. Options A/E remain possible future sources without a rewrite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The web build (`npm run build` → `dist/`) embeds the production residential pack (manifest, `cards.csv` and assets) with **no manual `<contentDir>/packs/` copy step**; a build-artefact assertion proves the pack is present in the emitted `dist/`.
- The pack-source abstraction resolves Main Street card-pack content from at least one non-Electron source (the bundled source) and is structured so a same-origin or remote source can be added **additively** without changing the core loader or the listing (the remote source itself is out of scope — `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).
- In the browser build (no `window.tce.contentDir` and no Electron bridges), Main Street boot discovers the bundled pack so the Card Packs panel lists the residential pack instead of "No card packs installed".
- The pack remains **gated** in the browser: while locked its cards stay out of play and its listing row offers a `[ Purchase ]` control.
- A **scoped simulated purchase** (declared rule `main-street-residential-pack-purchase`) flips the pack to unlocked and to `[ Enable ]`; enabling it merges its rows so its cards deal in play. A test covers the lock → purchase → enable → deal path in the browser source.
- The simulated purchase is **rule-scoped**: it does not collateral-unlock any other configured reward (for example the itch.io golf reward).
- Browser content-unlock state **persists across a page reload** through the `localStorage`-backed client, and the existing enabled-pack preference continues to persist.
- Pack CSV and asset URLs **resolve in the browser with no `tce-packs://` request**; either the bundled source supplies same-origin/relative URLs or the pack assets are demonstrably unused for card rendering.
- **Electron behaviour is unchanged**: with `window.tce.contentDir` set, discovery still reads the content directory through the existing `tce-packs://` protocol, and the content-directory install path remains supported.
- Save/load and missing/disabled-pack degradation continue to behave as they do under Electron, covered by focused browser-path regression tests.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (specifically `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change the Electron content-directory install path; it must remain
  supported (behavioural parity).
- The browser must remain functional with **no Electron bridges** — every new
  client degrades totally (never throws), matching the existing
  `createContentUnlockClient` / `loadCardPacks` total-degradation contract.
- Reuse existing seams (`StorageLike` in `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`;
  `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv`/`loader` overrides in `MainStreetCardPacks.ts`;
  the `virtual:game-registry` plugin pattern) rather than inventing parallel
  mechanisms.
- Pack content is bundled at build time — changing a bundled pack requires a
  rebuild in this iteration (runtime-updatable packs are the remote-source
  follow-up).
- Packs must stay licence-clean and project-generated (existing constraint from
  `packs/README.md`).
- The web base path is derived from the package name (GitHub Pages project
  site); any same-origin fallback must respect `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`.

## Out of scope

- Real storefront/Steam purchase wiring.
- A pack-authoring/store UI.
- Changing the Electron content-directory install path.
- Remote hosting of pack bundles (`MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`).
- Additional packs beyond the residential set.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — pack-source registry wiring; browser fallback
  content source; injected transports.
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` — wire the browser content-unlock client
  into entitlement resolution.
- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` — `localStorage`-backed unlock store (reusing
  `StorageLike`).
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — a bundled/localStorage-backed client
  compatible with the existing total client interface.
- `vite.config.ts` — pack bundling plugin (Option B) or a prebuild copy step.
- `core/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.*` — pattern reference for a
  `virtual:card-pack-registry` plugin (if Option B).
- `packs/` / `public/packs/` — bundled pack source/artefact.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — boot gate that must
  trigger discovery in the browser.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` / `core/src/ui/card-pack-url.ts` — URL
  resolution seam (avoid `tce-packs://` in the browser path).
- `tests/main-street/` — browser pack discovery, unlock/purchase persistence,
  and build-artefact tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` —
  docs.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep.** The registry abstraction invites building the remote source
  now. Mitigation: remote hosting stays a linked follow-up
  (`MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`); the abstraction only needs to admit it additively.
- **Supply-chain (future).** A remote pack injects card rows; the merge
  contract rejects bad headers/duplicate ids but not malicious content. The
  remote follow-up must add signing/hashing plus the unlock gate — recorded
  there, not built here.
- **Bundle size.** Option C always bundles every pack. Assumption: the single
  residential pack (10 cards + PNGs) is small enough; if it grows, Option B
  (opt-in registry) is available.
- **Duplicate unlock state.** A browser `localStorage` unlock client plus the
  Electron unified store could disagree. Assumption: the local client is used
  only when no Electron bridge is present; precedence is explicit and tested.
- **Gate semantics drift.** Bundling must not accidentally pre-unlock the pack
  (Option D's failure mode); the lock → purchase → enable assertions guard it.
- **Base-path correctness.** Same-origin URLs must work under the GitHub Pages
  project base (`/<package>/`), not just `/`.

## Related work

- **Parent context:** `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock
  and import (this item's discovery source).
- **Depends on / dependencies:**
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` — Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)
  **depends on this item** (blocked).
- **Related implementations:** `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H` (pack listing UI & boot
  wiring, completed), `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536` (pack merge & persistence,
  completed), `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6` (end-to-end pipeline test, completed),
  `MS-0MV16VYN3006SWM4` (content-unlock entitlement gate, open),
  `MS-0MV16VYYB000TI7H` (scoped simulated purchase, open),
  `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained, in progress).
- **Docs:** `packs/README.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV** – Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever after the rebalance (open)
- **MS-0MV1HAI5G005Q3RT** – [test-failure] composite-click.browser.test.ts > composite click deducts the premium for business and community-space cards via the dialog — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MUQZH6Z50035KVU** – Deployment documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, additional, also (+320 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, add, additional, also (+282 more)
- `core/README.md` — matched: add, also, always, appear, artefact (+193 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which pack-bundling mechanism should be used (Option A–E), and does it
  need to support remotely hosted bundles? — **Answer (producer, `MS-C0MV26XJNF00751OW` / `MS-C0MV26LA70005X6NS`):** Adopt a **pack-source registry**;
  build the abstraction now, implement the **bundled** source in this item
  (Option B or C), and leave remote hosting to the linked follow-up
  `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`. Option B alone cannot host remote bundles; remote is a
  runtime source the registry admits additively. Source: worklog comments.
- **Q:** How is the browser lock → purchase → enable flow preserved? —
  **Answer (producer, `MS-C0MV26XJNF00751OW`):** Add a **`localStorage`-backed
  content-unlock client** plus a client-side scoped simulated-purchase rule.
  Source: worklog comment.
- **Q:** Does this item change the Electron content-directory install path? —
  **Answer:** No; it remains supported and out of scope. Source: existing work
  item description ("Out of scope").
- **Q:** Should real storefront/Steam purchase be wired? — **Answer:** No;
  simulated purchase only, as elsewhere in the DLC pipeline. Source: existing
  work item description.

No open questions remain; the direction was locked by the producer on
2026-10-10.

# Console noise when running the tutorial (tf factory + zone collision warnings)

## Problem statement

Starting (and playing) the Main Street tutorial floods the browser console with developer warnings that are not actionable: `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory for key "income-positive-chime" ...` and repeated `Zone collision for "<hand|endTurnButton|incidentQueue>" while composing "main-street-canonical" with "main-street-tutorial" ...`. The noise obscures genuine errors and breaks "clean console" expectations for the tutorial boot path, while gameplay itself is unaffected.

Seed context: browser client console log captured while running the tutorial (`client:789`, 2026-10-10).

## Users

- **Developer / QA engineer** running the tutorial locally who needs a clean console so real errors are visible.
- **Automated browser tests / release checks** that treat unexpected console errors/warnings as failures.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want booting and playing the tutorial to emit no unexpected console warnings, so that any real error stands out immediately.
- As a QA engineer, I want the remaining intentional diagnostics to be explicit and quiet by default, so that I do not re-triage known-benign warnings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Booting/playing the tutorial at the canonical 1280×720 viewport emits **no** `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory ...` warning for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings (`sfx-income-positive`, `sfx-income-negative`, `sfx-income-neutral`, `sfx-challenge-complete`), while each of those keys still falls back to the WAV path (verified by test).
2. Booting the tutorial emits **no** `Zone collision ...` warning for `hand`, `endTurnButton`, or `incidentQueue` when composing `main-street-canonical` with `main-street-tutorial`, while the `sceneWins` result still resolves the tutorial zone rects (verified by test).
3. Unexpected diagnostics remain detectable: a genuinely missing factory or an unapproved zone collision can still be surfaced/asserted by tests rather than being silently swallowed (verified by test).
4. At least one regression test asserts the tutorial boot path produces no warnings from either source; `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`, `core/tests/ui/screen-layout-compose.test.ts`, and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` all still pass.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing WAV/Phaser fallback for factory-less SFX keys (engine contract CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76) — no silent drops.
- Do **not** add new ToneForge recipes/factories in this item (larger separate effort; see risks).
- Preserve `sceneWins` composition semantics and the tutorial alignment contract documented in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`; tutorial zone rects must not change.
- The fix must not blind future diagnostics — intentional cases are suppressed/deduplicated, not the detection removed.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tfAdapter.ts` (`createTfPlayer`) defaults to a `console.warn` logger. `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` calls `createTfPlayer(tfModule)` / `createTfPlayer(loadedModule)` without a logger, so every factory-less key warns on play.
- The committed runtime synth (`core/src/core-engine/tf-runtime/main-street-runtime-synth.mjs`) ships 12 factories, while `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` maps 16 logical keys; the 4 extra keys intentionally fall back to WAV (codified in `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`).
- `core/src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts` emits `ZONE_COLLISION` as `console.warn` when no `reportIssue` hook is supplied. `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (`resolveMarketCardAnchor` and `resolveZoneToAnchor`) calls `composeResolvedLayouts(BASE_LAYOUT, TUTORIAL_LAYOUT, …, { policy: 'sceneWins' })` with no hook, so the documented intentional overrides (`hand`, `endTurnButton`, `incidentQueue`, `developmentRow`) warn on every resolution.

## Desired change

- Make the intentional audio fallback silent (or debug-level, one-shot) in production wiring, while keeping the fallback behaviour and the ability to surface unexpected missing factories.
- Make the tutorial's known-intentional zone collisions quiet (e.g. via a `reportIssue` hook that ignores/deduplicates the documented override zones), while keeping unexpected collisions visible.
- Add regression tests pinning both.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — pass a quiet/debug logger to `createTfPlayer` at both call sites (~lines 253, ~278).
- `core/src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — keep the fallback path quiet/debug for known factory-less keys (~lines 300–330, 505–515).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — pass a `reportIssue` hook to both `composeResolvedLayouts` calls (~lines 159, ~203).
- `core/src/ui/screen-layout-compose.ts` — only if the composer needs a quiet/dedupe option; keep the public contract intact.
- `src/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` — annotate the four intentionally factory-less mappings.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`, `core/tests/ui/screen-layout-compose.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`, plus a tutorial boot console-cleanliness test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the four factory-less mappings are intended to use WAV fallback (evidence: `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` header + engine child CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76). We silence the warning rather than add synth factories.
- **Assumption:** tutorial zone-name reuse is intentional (evidence: alignment-contract comment in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`). We silence the intentional collision rather than rename zones.
- **Risk:** over-suppressing warnings hides a real missing factory / accidental collision. Mitigation: suppress only known keys/zones; add a test-visible reporter and keep unexpected issues visible.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adding the four missing synth factories (income positive/negative/neutral, challenge-complete) is a distinct, larger effort — record as a linked follow-up instead of expanding this item.
- **Risk:** console assertions are environment-sensitive; the regression test must target the specific warning messages, not "no console output at all".

## Related work

### Manual

- **MS-0MUU9QYQE006NLEZ** – Activate ToneForge runtime synth: loader diagnostics + scene wiring (completed) — established the fallback contract and diagnostics this item makes quiet. Engine sibling child: **CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76**.
- **MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42** – Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages) — release/web context.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42** – Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages) (completed)
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W** – Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (market weight / copies) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: client, collision, console, factory, noise, running, tutorial, when, zone
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: client, factory, running, tutorial, when, zone
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: console, factory, running, tutorial, when, zone

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed (browser console log) plus repository evidence determined scope and approach, and the resulting assumptions are documented above. Implicit questions resolved by research:

- Q: "Should the four factory-less SFX mappings gain ToneForge factories, or should the intentional WAV-fallback warning be silenced?" — Answer (agent research): silence/downgrade — `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts` explicitly codifies the four mappings as intentional WAV-fallback cases (engine contract CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76). Source: repo evidence, `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`.
- Q: "Should tutorial zone names be renamed to avoid collisions, or should the intentional collisions be quiet?" — Answer (agent research): keep the names and quiet the warning — `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` documents `sceneWins` override of `hand`/`endTurnButton`/`incidentQueue` as an intentional alignment contract. Source: repo evidence, `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (~lines 40–80).

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)

**Related:** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (Make card packs available in the browser
distribution — introduces the pack-source registry this builds on)
**Related:** `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (Make card-pack assets self-contained)

## Summary

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, once `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` lands, a bundled
build-time registry. This item adds a **remote pack source** so a pack catalogue
can be hosted at a URL and fetched at runtime — enabling packs to be published
or updated without rebuilding or re-releasing the game.

This is the future-work half of the source-registry design: the registry seam
(`PackSource[]`) is introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`, and this item
implements the remote provider on top of it.

## Goal (user story)

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack (and its catalogue) at
> a URL, so I can publish or update packs for an installed game without
> rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want a remote pack to appear in the Card Packs panel and
> behave exactly like a bundled or content-directory pack (lock → purchase →
> enable → deal), while the game still boots and plays offline on its bundled
> packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` that fetches a pack
   manifest from a configured URL (via the loader's existing `fetchManifest` /
   `fetchCsv` transports) and contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Define how remote source URLs are declared — a build-time
   config constant, a launcher-provided setting, or a well-known manifest URL —
   and how multiple remote sources compose with bundled/static ones.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Define ordering and conflict handling when the same
   pack id appears in more than one source (bundled wins? first wins? reject
   duplicates?). The core merge contract already rejects duplicate card ids
   whole; pack-id precedence must be decided explicitly.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Decide whether remote
   packs may be ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable or serving a
   malformed manifest must degrade to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never block boot, never blank the listing. Define a timeout.
6. **Trust and integrity.** Address the supply-chain surface: remote packs
   inject card rows into the pool, and the merge contract validates the header
   and duplicate ids but not malicious content. Define an integrity mechanism
   (signing, checksum pinning, allow-listed host/ids) and what the game does
   when verification fails.
7. **Caching / offline.** Decide whether remote packs are cached (for example in
   `localStorage` / Cache Storage) so a previously fetched pack remains usable
   offline, and how cache invalidation/versioning works.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, degradation, gating and
   integrity with tests, and document the remote-hosting contract.

## Acceptance criteria (to be confirmed at intake)

1. A pack catalogue hosted at a configured URL is discovered at runtime and its
   packs appear in the Card Packs panel.
2. Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across lock → purchase →
   enable → deal, and save/load.
3. With the remote host unreachable/slow, the game boots on bundled packs and
   warns; the listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad header/duplicate id is
   rejected whole with a warning, without affecting other sources.
5. Pack-id precedence across sources is deterministic and documented.
6. The integrity mechanism rejects a tampered/unverified remote pack and
   documents the failure mode.
7. Remote pack art resolves and renders (coordinated with
   `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`).
8. Documentation covers configuration, the hosting contract, integrity and
   degradation.
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline (a natural follow-up).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; without integrity
  checks a hostile pack could inject arbitrary card data. Mitigation: signing /
  checksum pinning / host allow-list, with a safe refusal mode.
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the game.
  Mitigation: bounded timeout, non-blocking discovery, bundled-first.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack may lose
  it offline. Mitigation: explicit caching decision.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than re-architecting.

## Key files (predicted)
